sources: dossier=Required behaviors: 'message_type on the subscription is validated against the target instance's message registry; the legacy single-valued invalidate kind is retired (2026-06-14, bfc9febb, transcript)' — silent on timing/failure-mode specifics; doc=invariant (old line 34) claimed the check runs 'at the publisher-subscription's mounting time' and mismatches 'keep the row in the mounting state' with 'the failed-reason field' carrying the diagnostic; code=validatePublishers in the template validator (@concept: message-schema) rejects an undeclared message_type as a template ValidationError — the template is refused outright, no instance or row is ever created; reconcileMountingSubscriptionsOnce performs no message-type check; FailureReason is written only together with a transition to Failed (markSubscriptionFailed), never while a row stays mounting; test=none located for a mounting+failed-reason co-state (it is unreachable in the state machine).
note: Dossier confirms message_type validation against the registry is real intent but is silent on timing; code proves it happens at template-validation time and the doc's 'mounting + failed-reason' state is unrepresentable. Doc corrected to describe the actual template-validation-time rejection and to disambiguate it from the mounting-to-failed lifecycle invariant.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Instance termination reads nothing about publisher-subscriptions (2026-06-03 invariant)'; Corrections record: the NOT-EXISTS termination-gating clause 'was explicitly reverted (2026-06-03)... termination reads nothing about subscriptions' — precedent that coupling termination to subscription state is forbidden; doc=Definition (old line 11) said the row is 'dropped at instance termination'; doc's own Invariant (line 35, unchanged) already correctly says 'the stopped state is reached on unsubscribe'; code=handleTerminateInstance and handleDeleteInstance both call StopPublisherSubscriptionsForInstance, which flips active/mounting rows to stopped via markSubscriptionStopped — the row persists, is not deleted; no non-test caller of the Delete method exists; test=none needed, internal doc contradiction (line 11 vs line 35) plus code both settle it.
note: Termination not 'reading' subscription state (the 2026-06-03 invariant, about gating) is distinct from termination writing a stopped transition as a side effect (which is real and intended, per the doc's own unchanged lifecycle invariant). Definition line corrected from 'dropped' to 'transitions to stopped ... row is retained, not deleted', resolving the doc's internal inconsistency.

sources: dossier=publisher-subscription.md Required behaviors and publisher.md Net position both assert 'reconciliation worker retries mounting subscriptions forever with backoff', both citing the same single artifact (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability) — not independent corroboration, and the entry's own quoted transcript fragment ('retry-forever matches desired-state semantics; bounded budgets convert contention spikes into silent failures') supports only the no-attempt-cap half of the claim, not backoff; doc=invariant (line 35, unchanged) says the reconciler drives mounting rows 'with backoff and no attempt cap'; code=RunPublisherSubscriptionReconciler uses a fixed time.NewTicker(interval) and reconcileMountingSubscriptionsOnce makes one flat-interval Subscribe attempt per row per tick with no per-row backoff state or schema column; the exponential-backoff helper (callSubscribeWithRetry, pow28) exists but is invoked only by ResyncPublisherSubscriptions at startup, never by the steady-state reconciler; test=none found asserting reconciler backoff behavior.
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): the reconciler's 'with backoff' clause was dossier/decision distillation drift — its sole artifact source evidences only the no-attempt-cap property. The flat fixed-interval retry-forever behavior is ratified as intent; per-row backoff is explicitly not required (revisit only with real outage evidence). 'With backoff' dropped from publisher-subscription.md, decision:subscription-reconciler, and both dossier entries. Concept invariant wording fixed.

sources: dossier=silent on any by-publisher operator listing capability; Required behaviors mentions only 'per-subscription state is visible on the instance-detail surface' (per-instance, not per-publisher); dossier's Intentional absences also does not list this as a deliberately-dropped capability, so it was never promised in the first place; doc=invariant (old line 33) justified the composite identity with 'operators can scan one publisher's subscriptions efficiently'; the doc's own Boundaries section (line 25, unchanged) independently describes the same composite identity without this claim; code=the composite PRIMARY KEY (publisher_name, id) exists in the schema, but PublisherSubscriptionsTable exposes only ListByInstance and ListByState — no ListByPublisher; the only operator read surface lists per-instance; test=none.
note: The composite identity itself is real and correctly described elsewhere in the doc; only the 'operators can scan efficiently' rationale is an unbuilt, unpromised capability. Reworded the invariant to state the identity's actual purpose (independent per-publisher subscription-id namespacing) without the unsupported operator-surface claim.

sources: dossier=same as row 539 — Required behaviors: message_type validated against the target instance's message registry (2026-06-14, bfc9febb, transcript), silent on timing; dossier does not describe any mounting-time check nor a mounting+failed-reason composite state; code=neither StartPublisherSubscriptionsForInstance nor reconcileMountingSubscriptionsOnce inspects MessageType against the template's messages registry; the only check is validatePublishers at template-validation/registration time; the doc's described state combination is unrepresentable in the persistence layer's state model; test=none for a mounting+failed-reason state (unreachable).
note: Same underlying defect as row 539 (same doc line, same invariant); ruling and the doc edit are shared with 539's fix — the invariant now states the message-type check happens at template validation and is disambiguated from the separate mounting-to-failed lifecycle invariant.
